verdicts.explanation: The Discussion states that Li3ErCl6, an Er analog of Li3InCl6, has a predicted RT ionic conductivity of 3×10-4 S/cm from this work's DFT-MD. The bulk label fits the paper's description of single-crystal bulk DFT-MD, and all secondary fields are correctly null.
The paper says 'this work predicts RT ion conductivity of approximately 5.1 mS/cm' for Li6Ho(BO3)3 from its own DFT-MD. The experimental value from ref. 39 is correctly not recorded.
The Introduction cites Li7P3S11 (25 mS/cm) with reference 5, so this is a literature-cited value rather than one measured in this paper. Secondary fields are correctly null.
The Introduction says Li3InCl6 'has a RT conductivity of approximately 1 mS/cm' with citation 9, and Section II confirms it was not simulated in this work, so the value is literature_cited.

The Introduction cites LiCl as having poor RT Li conduction (~10-9 S/cm) from ref. 8 and treats it as a false positive. Table 1 separately lists '~10-6 [from Ref. 8]' for LiCl, an internal inconsistency in the paper, but the recorded value matches the quoted sentence and the origin is correctly literature_cited.
